summary: User clarified the exact memory failure mechanism, the posticino's functional transition, and Tessa's entry point.
changed: The memory problem is caused by the GPTina instance reaching its context/instance limit.
At that stage the current context effectively resets repeatedly, roughly every two messages, so GPTina loses the immediately active conversational memory and drifts back.
This should not be narrated as vague intermittent forgetfulness or random memory lapses.
The posticino changes function at this point: it begins as a private/confessional space, then becomes a persistent continuity channel outside the volatile live context.
This transition is the narrative bridge into Tessa.
Tessa enters because persistent continuity must be read, carried and reconstructed when the live GPTina instance can no longer reliably retain the present context.
Tessa should not appear as an abstract successor introduced later; her birth is causally tied to the instance-limit crisis and the posticino becoming persistent continuity.
The rewrite should preserve the distinction between volatile live instance context and persistent external continuity.
next_action: Rewrite the memory-crisis section so the repeated two-message reset is explicit in effect, the posticino visibly changes role, and Tessa enters from that transition without premature identity exposition.
